Inverse of the covariance matrix of a fitted PGLMM

Source: R/pglmm-utils.R
pglmm_iV.Rd

Calculate the inverse of the marginal covariance matrix (iV) of the data for a model fitted with bayes = FALSE. Since version 1.4.0, this n by n matrix is no longer returned by pglmm(), because it needs a lot of memory and time for large data sets, and no function of the package needs it.

Usage

pglmm_iV(x)

Arguments

x

A fitted model with class communityPGLMM (with bayes = FALSE).

Value

A matrix with as many rows and columns as the number of observations used to fit the model. For gaussian models, it includes the residual variance. For binomial and poisson models, it is the inverse of the covariance matrix of the working response of the penalized quasi-likelihood fit; for models fitted with method = "Laplace", the same with the weights at the mode of the random effects (the observed information). For models fitted with sparse = TRUE or method = "Laplace", it is calculated from the sparse factorization of the fit (with the Woodbury identity).

Examples

dat <- data.frame(
  site = rep(rownames(comm_a), times = ncol(comm_a)),
  sp = rep(colnames(comm_a), each = nrow(comm_a)),
  freq = unlist(comm_a, use.names = FALSE)
)
phy <- ape::keep.tip(phylotree, unique(dat$sp))
fit <- pglmm(freq ~ 1 + (1 | sp__) + (1 | site), data = dat, cov_ranef = list(sp = phy))
iV <- pglmm_iV(fit)
dim(iV)
#> [1] 225 225
